indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the words before it are smashed and rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A weary walker finishes a long, exhausting trudge completely worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull, slow and uninspired is called pedestrian, a figurative sense of walking pace.

clue.text: Beginning of podcast on the radio

definitions.text: Beginning of podcast on the radio

blocks.note: surface reading: the opening minutes of an audio show being broadcast
setter's reading: the first letter of podcast as it is called in the radio operators' spelling alphabet

explanation.surface: A podcast's opening is being played out over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATO phonetic alphabet, used by radio operators, gives each letter a code word; the first letter of podcast is P, whose code word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the international radio spelling alphabet the code word standing for the letter P is this one.

indicators.note: a vacated building has had its contents removed, so only the shell of the word is kept

blocks.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a daily is a cleaning lady, also called a char
just the first and last letters of the word give

explanation.surface: Police officers hand over a newspaper and an empty building on their release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper but is a British word for a cleaner who comes in every day.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a prisoner or patient is to let them go, so the noun means a freeing or letting out.

indicators.note: anything on board a vessel is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship, opening around its contents
to bug someone is to pester or nag them

explanation.surface: An insect is spotted crawling on the deck of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Snags are hitches or hidden drawbacks, the same sense as a catch in a deal.

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read from bottom to top
in places the reversed word inside the outer word

blocks.note: a tirade is a rant, which opens to take the insert
support is aid, read upwards

explanation.surface: A speaker's furious outburst wins applause and backing from the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant means shining brightly, so it matches brilliant in its sense of glowing light or radiance.

clue.text: Most copious section of samples taken

indicators.note: a section is a slice cut out of something larger, so the letters run inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters sits across the two words

explanation.surface: A researcher draws the largest share from a batch of specimens collected.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, so its superlative describes the greatest abundance or plenty.

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
AM is the abbreviation for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Someone runs naked across a pitch during a live morning broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streak' suggests running naked, but here it is a narrow line of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is a narrow ray or shaft of light, a bright line crossing a space.

blocks.note: the heart of the word sweet is its central letter
lite is the commercial spelling for a low-calorie dieting product

explanation.surface: A partner trying to slim is offered a dessert with cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best members, the choicest people, just as this word denotes the top tier.

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn and gathered in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written into the fodder
taken as written into the fodder

explanation.surface: A TV contest is shown in which a painter is assessed.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a lay or minor judicial officer who sits in court and tries lesser cases.

clue.text: Dish finished before end of tea

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so just that one is kept

blocks.note: something finished is over and past
the closing letter of tea

explanation.surface: A meal is cleared away before teatime is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti or penne makes a meal, so the Italian staple works as an example of a plated course.

indicators.note: to snatch is to grab and hold, so the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: darting is running quickly, split to take the insert
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A thief heads off at a sprint, grabbing an album on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone departing is leaving or starting a journey, so it matches setting off on the way.

clue.text: It could be the main event?

definitions.text: It could be the main event?

blocks.note: surface reading: the headline attraction on a programme
setter's reading: the main is an old word for the open sea, so this is a gathering held on water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' as the high sea is a poetic usage; the question mark signals that the obvious meaning of main event is a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of boat or yacht races is a sporting meet on the water, an event on the sea.

blocks.note: HO is an abbreviation for house
a stage is a raised platform

explanation.surface: Guards protect a raised stand outside a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the house before the platform here, as in an across clue where one thing follows on.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held as a pledge or guarantee that terms will be met, so a form of collateral.

clue.text: Give unverified estimate, say, sketchy initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each preceding word

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone offers a rough, unchecked figure that is admittedly vague.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the word from its first letters and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to offer a rough answer without proof, a figure that is uncertain and loosely reckoned.

blocks.note: first meaning: rise in value, as property may
second meaning: to value or treasure highly

explanation.surface: A contestant wonders whether to climb the stage to collect an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' reads as a noun for an award, but it is the verb meaning to value.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets increase in worth over time, and people value what they treasure; the same verb covers both.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
follows puts the drink after the shortened word

blocks.note: neat, of a drink, means pure and undiluted
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A glass of wine is taken after a nearly undiluted shot of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' seems to be the liquor in the surface, but it means the gist of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The purport of a text is its general meaning or thrust, as in the spirit rather than the letter of it.

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
providing in the sense of on condition that
to chill a drink is to ice it

explanation.surface: Elite troops are supplying the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective for elite troops, but it is a noun for a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening or hole, so a crack or slit in a surface fits it.

clue.text: More ragged cheers time before row

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks
T is the symbol for time
a tier is a row or level of seats

explanation.surface: Raggedy fans cheer loudly before a quarrel breaks out in the stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby and worn, so the comparative describes something more threadbare and frayed.

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters run inside the next words

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the three words

explanation.surface: A fool may be either spiteful or entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant or stupid person, a dunce, so it pairs with a fool or idiot.

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it within, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a ring is a round shape, opening to take the insert
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler swims about while landing a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' is not about water: a head that swims is dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: When your head is swimming you feel dizzy and unsteady, staggering and spinning as if about to fall.

clue.text: Prattle about left being more plausible

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the second

blocks.note: to gibber is to prattle nonsense, opening to take the insert
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Idle chatter about the political left proves more convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib talk sounds smooth and slick, so the comparative means more fluent and superficially convincing.

indicators.note: in puts the first word inside the following words

blocks.note: a, plus ST as the abbreviation for street
to gather is to gain or collect

explanation.surface: Protesters assemble on a road, standing firm against the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is opposing or fighting it, the stance of someone who resists.

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters take an irregular order

blocks.note: taken as written into the fodder
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A play is unexpectedly given a new cast, with an understudy stepping in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recast' looks like the anagram signal in a theatre surface, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman who acts on stage or screen, one kind of entertainer or player.

indicators.note: first means the second word goes ahead of the first in the build

blocks.note: a fleece is an animal's woolly coat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A creature has a single woolly jacket to its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted raccoon relative of the Americas, a mammal with a ringed tail.

blocks.note: AC is short for account, as in a/c
to empty a place is to clear or rid it

explanation.surface: A customer is resentful on discovering the bank balance is zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' tempts you to drop the middle letters of account, but it is a verb giving letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid taste or smell is sharp and harsh, close to bitter, which is why 'perhaps' hedges the link.

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the team's name encloses the other word

blocks.note: Inter is the Milan football club, opening to take the insert
EG, for example, stands for say

explanation.surface: An Italian football club fields a team of eleven players.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven looks like a football side, but it is just a number, and the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a whole number, and any whole number is an example of this mathematical term.

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inside, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of garden
ash is the residue left after burning

explanation.surface: Someone pulverises the leftover rubbish from a cleared vegetable plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind one's teeth together, in anger or pain.

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A silent figure sometimes manages to write verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric verses addressed to a subject, a classic form of poetry.

clue.text: About in time, fit and willing

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the following word

blocks.note: an age is a period of time, opening to take the insert
re means about or concerning
fit to do something means able to

explanation.surface: Someone is ready and keen, roughly on schedule and in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreeable person is ready to consent or go along with something, so happy and prepared.

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: wounded means hurt or harmed

explanation.surface: An injured fighter, decapitated, still carries a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, but this clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be armed is to carry guns or other arms, equipped for fighting.

blocks.note: first meaning: goals or purposes, as in means to an end
second meaning: finishes off, as one does a life

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the armed fighter of the previous clue, so aims and kills look like gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means purposes or objectives, while the verb means puts a stop to something, including a life.

clue.text: Dislocated hip, so rests hip replacement?

indicators.note: a dislocated joint is knocked out of position, so the letters are moved out of their order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A patient with a damaged hip takes it easy while awaiting new surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is an example: a replacement hip is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial body part fitted to replace a missing or damaged one is called by this medical term.
